newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian anglers spend cold night trapped on ice.
newsitem.headline: Canadian anglers spend cold night trapped on ice.

text.p: About 200 fishermen and snowmobilers were forced to spend a cold and windy night trapped on ice floes on a lake about 45 miles (70 km) north of Toronto, police said on Sunday.

At least 700 people had been stranded during an ice-fishing derby on Saturday after several huge cracks -- one more than seven miles (11 km) and at least 100 yards (metres) wide in spots -- broke through the thick ice on Lake Simcoe.

Police and military emergency crews used helicopters and boats to bring people ashore, but poor visibility from snow squalls and high winds forced the rescuers to close down their operations during the night, police said.
About 200 people remained to be rescued on Sunday, and no injuries had been reported, police said. They said they were confident the remaining anglers would be brought to safety.
"Most of them have heaters in their fish huts, and if they didn't, they should have been responsible enough to break into a hut with heat," said one officer.

A thin skin of ice had formed over the open sections of water by Sunday morning, making boat rescue efforts difficult, but helicopters circled over the area to pick up the remaining anglers, police said.
Some people had no idea they were in danger until they saw the helicopters overhead, local radio stations reported.

"When the (fishing) lines were all slanted in the hut ... it was just like the hut was moving," fisherman Tom Slade told Canadian Press. "I had to wake my partners up. I said 'Something's wrong here.'"

The ice was about eight inches (20 cm) thick in most places and had been considered safe for fishing and even driving, but strong currents and vicious winds pushed large pieces of ice away from shore, said Ontario Provincial Police Sergeant Dana Morris in nearby Orillia.
"This is a rather freak situation," he said. "The winds drove the ice floes from the main portion of the ice."
